newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Roman, Russian churches discuss historic meeting.
newsitem.headline: Roman, Russian churches discuss historic meeting.

text.p: The Patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church may meet Pope John Paul in Austria later this month in an unprecedented encounter between the two Christian leaders, a Russian church official said on Friday.
"Talks are now being held between the Vatican and the Patriarchate in Moscow," said Timofei Zolotusky, an official in the Patriarchate external relations department.
"In all of history there has never been such a meeting," Zolotusky said. "Since talks are being held, it shows that both sides want it to happen."
Officials are hoping to arrange the meeting between Pope John Paul II and Patriarch Alexiy II in Vienna on June 21 ahead of the European Ecumenical Conference in Graz.
Austrian officials say the Ecumenical Patriarch of Istanbul Bartholomew I, who met the Pope in 1995, may also attend the meeting.

Christendom, long divided between western churches looking to Rome and the eastern church based in Byzantium -- now Istanbul -- finally split in the Great Schism 1054, though the churches still say reunification remains a long-term goal.

The Pope has expressed a desire to travel to Russia, where eastern Christianity was introduced less than a century before the Schism. But the Russian Church, sensitive to the influx of rival religions in recent years, has opposed such a visit.
